Ecosystem watch: **[verso](/?date=2026-10-01&category=research#item-hn-49628094)**, a free open-source orchestrator for knowledge work built on top of Hermes Agent, signals an application layer forming around the project — third parties now treat Hermes as a platform, not a single tool. Net read: no merged PRs, official news-channel items, social posts, or Reddit threads this cycle — the **v0.20.0** announcement (pending tag verification) is the ship of record — and no new model launches. top_items.author: HF Daily Papers
top_items.summary: Research paper examining skill retrieval for LLM agents as skill marketplaces grow past 230,000 reusable SKILL.md packages in the Agent Skills format. The authors argue that selection, not authoring, is now the bottleneck, and critique the standard approach of LLM-mediated retrieval loops that rewrite queries and refine candidates inside the agent decision loop, which costs tokens on every task. They introduce SkillSeek, an open-source two-stage skill retrieval approach that moves selection out of the agent loop.

top_items.title: ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes Agent: Paid vs Free
top_items.content:
ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes is really a question of philosophy. Dots are OpenAI’s polished, paid, always-on agents living inside ChatGPT. Hermes Agent is the free, open-source agent I run my whole operation on, living on my own machine with whatever model I choose. When I tested Dots on launch day (above), my honest reaction was that it feels like “a version of Hermes Agent for beginners that’s still not that smooth.” Here’s the full comparison.

Key takeaways

- Dots: paid, managed, beginner-friendly — GPT-6 Astra, own cloud computer, 4,000+ apps, inside ChatGPT.

- Hermes: free and open source — runs on your machine, any model (local or cloud), bot mode, Bot Screen, voice.

- Control: Hermes gives you everything — models, data, plugins; Dots gives you Custom Rules within OpenAI’s walls.

- My take: Dots is easier to start; Hermes is more capable, cheaper and yours.

## ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes side by side

## ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes in practice

Dots win on first-run experience: open ChatGPT, name your Dot, pick an avatar, done. For someone who’s never touched an agent, that matters. But in my test the experience fell apart on real work — slow computer use, a call feature that didn’t connect, images that wouldn’t load, and app connections hidden away.

Hermes asks more of you up front, then gives you more: pick the best model for each job, run it locally for privacy, watch it on its own screen, talk to it hands-free, and keep every session in your own vault. No regional restrictions, no plan tiers, no waiting for a beta to settle. That’s why I run my business on it.

Want this working in your business, not just bookmarked? Setting up Hermes Agent as your always-on AI team is exactly the kind of thing we build together inside the AI Profit Boardroom — 3,400+ members, four live calls a week, daily Q&A, the Agent OS and Hermes kits, and a 30-day roadmap so you ship instead of watch.

Prefer it mapped 1-on-1 first? Book a free strategy session and we’ll plan it for your exact situation.

Join the AI Profit Boardroom →Book a Free Strategy Session →

## Who should pick which

- Never used an agent, happy to pay, outside Europe: Dots is the gentlest start.

- Want control, privacy or zero subscription: Hermes, no contest.

- In the UK or EU: Dots on Pro isn’t available at launch — Hermes works anywhere.

- Want the best of both: run Hermes with a flagship model like Claude Opus 5.5 for heavy jobs.

Sourcing, dated 30 September 2026: Dots facts are from OpenAI’s DevDay launch (29 September 2026) as reported by TechCrunch and DataCamp’s explainer; test observations are from my own hands-on session in the video above, on day one of the rollout. Early-rollout bugs (like the call button) may be fixed quickly — I’ll update this page as they are.

## The bottom line on ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes

ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes: Dots is the easy, paid, managed option that’s still rough on day one; Hermes is the free, open, more capable agent you control completely. If you’re willing to spend an hour on setup, Hermes wins — and it doesn’t care what plan or country you’re in. Full Dots review: ChatGPT Dots, tested.

## Where ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes is closer than it looks

To be fair to Dots, a few things it ships on day one take real work to match in Hermes. Its Custom Rules give non-technical users a clean approval model — act alone, act if pre-approved, ask first, or escalate — and sensitive actions like password changes always need your sign-off. It connects to 4,000+ apps through OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem, keeps memories between conversations, and you can message your Dot from ChatGPT on desktop, web or mobile, with Slack and Teams too.

Hermes can do all of that — approvals through your config, integrations through its connectors and MCP servers, memory through your own vault — but you assemble it rather than switch it on. So the honest framing is: Dots trades control and cost for convenience. If convenience is what you’re short of, that trade can make sense; if control or budget matters more, Hermes is the better long-term home.

## FAQ: chatgpt dots vs hermes

### What’s the difference between ChatGPT Dots and Hermes Agent?

Dots are paid, managed always-on agents inside ChatGPT running on OpenAI’s cloud; Hermes is a free, open-source agent that runs on your own machine with any model you choose.

### Is Hermes Agent free?

top_items.content_html:
ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes is really a question of philosophy. Dots are OpenAI’s polished, paid, always-on agents living inside ChatGPT. Hermes Agent is the free, open-source agent I run my whole operation on, living on my own machine with whatever model I choose. When I tested Dots on launch day (above), my honest reaction was that it feels like “a version of Hermes Agent for beginners that’s still not that smooth.” Here’s the full comparison.

Key takeaways

  • Dots: paid, managed, beginner-friendly — GPT-6 Astra, own cloud computer, 4,000+ apps, inside ChatGPT.
  • Hermes: free and open source — runs on your machine, any model (local or cloud), bot mode, Bot Screen, voice.
  • Control: Hermes gives you everything — models, data, plugins; Dots gives you Custom Rules within OpenAI’s walls.
  • My take: Dots is easier to start; Hermes is more capable, cheaper and yours.

ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes in practice

Dots win on first-run experience: open ChatGPT, name your Dot, pick an avatar, done. For someone who’s never touched an agent, that matters. But in my test the experience fell apart on real work — slow computer use, a call feature that didn’t connect, images that wouldn’t load, and app connections hidden away.

Hermes asks more of you up front, then gives you more: pick the best model for each job, run it locally for privacy, watch it on its own screen, talk to it hands-free, and keep every session in your own vault. No regional restrictions, no plan tiers, no waiting for a beta to settle. That’s why I run my business on it.

Who should pick which

  • Never used an agent, happy to pay, outside Europe: Dots is the gentlest start.
  • Want control, privacy or zero subscription: Hermes, no contest.
  • In the UK or EU: Dots on Pro isn’t available at launch — Hermes works anywhere.
  • Want the best of both: run Hermes with a flagship model like Claude Opus 5.5 for heavy jobs.

Sourcing, dated 30 September 2026: Dots facts are from OpenAI’s DevDay launch (29 September 2026) as reported by TechCrunch and DataCamp’s explainer; test observations are from my own hands-on session in the video above, on day one of the rollout. Early-rollout bugs (like the call button) may be fixed quickly — I’ll update this page as they are.

The bottom line on ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes

ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes: Dots is the easy, paid, managed option that’s still rough on day one; Hermes is the free, open, more capable agent you control completely. If you’re willing to spend an hour on setup, Hermes wins — and it doesn’t care what plan or country you’re in. Full Dots review: ChatGPT Dots, tested.

Where ChatGPT Dots vs Hermes is closer than it looks

To be fair to Dots, a few things it ships on day one take real work to match in Hermes. Its Custom Rules give non-technical users a clean approval model — act alone, act if pre-approved, ask first, or escalate — and sensitive actions like password changes always need your sign-off. It connects to 4,000+ apps through OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem, keeps memories between conversations, and you can message your Dot from ChatGPT on desktop, web or mobile, with Slack and Teams too.

Hermes can do all of that — approvals through your config, integrations through its connectors and MCP servers, memory through your own vault — but you assemble it rather than switch it on. So the honest framing is: Dots trades control and cost for convenience. If convenience is what you’re short of, that trade can make sense; if control or budget matters more, Hermes is the better long-term home.
